sentences.text: Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal

This appeal is filed by the appellant being aggrieved of the judgment of conviction and sentence dated 4/12/2023 passed by the learned 1st Additional Sessions Judge Kotma, District Anuppur in S.C. No.2/2022 whereby sole appellant has been convicted under Section 5 (M)6 of POCSO Act, 2012, Section 376, 376(2)(f) and 376 (AB) of I.P.C. and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years and fine of Rs.5000/- with default stipulation of six months R.I.
2.

entities.text: 1st Additional Sessions Judge Kotma, District Anuppur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated.

It is further submitted that if statements of mother of the prosecutrix as were given under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. before the concerned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Kotma NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:30873 2 CRA-524-2024 are taken into consideration, then mother of the prosecutrix has stated that on 8/12/2021, the appellant was trying to violate the privacy of the prosecutrix.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class, Kotma NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: When she called the prosecutrix, then she came out from the terrace and stated that neighbourer was doing bad work to her.
When she asked as to what was being done, then prosecutrix/victim stated that her chest was being pressed and he had taken out underwear.
At that time, her husband was on duty.
When he returned back, then on the next day, a report was lodged at Police Station Bijuri.

This statement is contained in Ex. P-6.

sentences.text: Similarly, father of the prosecutrix gave his statements as contained in Ex. P-8 and stated that when he came back from duty, then he had asked her daughter as to what had happened, then she stated that uncle was doing wrong.
Then, she said that uncle had called her in the terrace and pressed her hands and feet.

4. Thus, it is submitted that it is by no stretch of imagination, her case falls under Section 3 or Section 5 of the POCSO Act and at best, even if the statement of mother is accepted to be correct,
then that will be the case of sexual assault as defined under Section 7 of the POCSO Act punishable under Section 8 with minimum punishment of three years and maximum of five years.
5. Learned Public Prosecutor Shri Ajay Tamrakar supports the impugned judgment of conviction and submits that age of the prosecutrix at the time of the incident was hardly ten years.

It is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:30873 3 CRA-524-2024 submitted that date of birth of the prosecutrix is proved through her birth certificate prepared by the Registrar (Birth and Death),
Gram Panchayat Kotma, Janpad Panchayat Anuppur, District Anuppur showing her date of birth as 16/03/2012.
This fact is further corroborated through Ex. A-2 which is her report card from Class-I to Class-V in which again her date of birth is mentioned as 16/03/2012.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, it is evident that PW-1 mother of the prosecutrix after having said that age of the prosecutrix is about ten years stated that appellant is her neighbourer.

He is residing in the neigbourhood in the house given by S.E.C.L.
There are neigbourers in the third floor of the building.

She stated that the appellant had tried to violate her privacy and then stated in the examination-in-chief that the appellant had taken the prosecutrix for pressing of his feet and then stated that he had pressed her chest and had tried to violate her privacy.
She admits that she had given statements under Section 164 of Cr.P.C as contained in Ex. P-6 which contains her signatures and she had narrated everything about the incident in her 164 statements.
7. In the cross-examination PW-1 admits that terrace is common and employees of the colliery and their family members keep visiting that terrace.
In para 3, this witness admitted that when children play on the terrace and talk, then their sound is audible till her room.
She admitted that she had not heard any of the cries of the victim.
She further NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:30873 4 CRA-524-2024 admitted that she had not given any intimation about the crime to any of her neighbourers.
She further admitted that on the next day, her husband had returned from duty at about 10:30 P.M.
Then, she had narrated everything to her husband.
Father of the prosecutrix admitted that there is a common passage which is open to all the persons of the colony and nobody can travel upto the terrace.

He admits that no seizure was made from the appellant and when he had signed Ex. P-7 i.e. the property seizure memo, at that time, the appellant was not present.
9. PW-3 prosecutrix had given her statements under Section 164 which have been exhibited as Ex.
P-11 before the Judicial Magistrate First Class.
She improvised her statements deposing before the court and stated that her chest was pressed and appellant tried to touch her vagina with his pennis.

sentences.text: She also stated that she was crying and was not feeling comfortable and, therefore, she came out and informed her mother.
This witness also admitted that when she plays on the terrace with other children, then the sound is audible in her flat.

10. PW-4 Rajesh Kumar Kashyap stated that the prosecutrix is his niece and the appellant had raped her.
11. PW-5 Sanjay Kumar Kashyap stated that father of the victim is his cousin brother and he had visited the house of the victim when he had received a telephone call.
12. PW-6 brother of the victim stated that the appellant was pressing NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:30873 5 CRA-524-2024 feet of the victim and was pressing her chest.
When his sister asked him to leave her, then her sister ran down and came to the house.
Dr. Deeparani Tudo Lady Doctor at Community Health Center, Kotma stated that she was posted as Medical Officer.
On production of the victim by the Woman Constable, she had carried out medical examination of the victim after obtaining consent of her parents.
She had not found any injury on the visible parts of body of the victim.
On internal examination, it was found that all the genitals were normal.
No opinion about immediate intercourse can be given.
In the cross-examination, she admitted that there were no injury signs on any parts of body of the victim.

14. Thus, when evidence of all the prosecution witnesses is taken into consideration along with the fact that PW-8 Lady Doctor has clearly opined that there were no signs of any injury, therefore,
when Ex. P-6 and P-8 are read, then it is evident that both the parents improvised their statements under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
There is no F.S.L. report available on record to substantiate any of the findings of violation of privacy.
There are no statements under Section 161.
Statements are exhibited.
F.S.L. report though not exhibited reveals that human sperms were not found on any of the Articles.

15. When these facts are taken into consideration, then appellant is guilty of pressing the chest of the prosecutrix, that will come under the definition of sexual assault as defined under Section 7 of the POCSO NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:30873 6 CRA-524-2024 Act.

entities.text: POCSO NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:30873 6 CRA-524-2024 Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: There is no evidence of either penetrative sexual assault or aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
16. When these facts are taken into consideration, then appellant's conviction under Sections 5(M)6 of POCSO Act 2012, 376, 376(2)(f) and 376 (AB) of I.P.C. cannot be sustained.

It is altered to Section 7 of POCSO Act and he is directed to undergo sentence of four years R.I. and fine of Rs.5,000/- with default stipulation of two months R.I.
17.
In above terms, the appeal is disposed of.
18. Case property be disposed of in terms of the directions of the trial court.
19. Record of the trial court be sent back.
